audits.title: Improving adherence to lung cancer guidelines: a quality improvement project that uses chart review, audit and feedback approach.
audits.standard: Lung cancer clinical practice guidelines: pathological diagnosis, staging before treatment, tumour board within 30 days of diagnosis, EGFR testing, end-of-life care
audits.setting: Department of Oncology, Ministry of the National Guard - Health Affairs, Riyadh (tertiary)

cycle1.result: Histological subtype identified 94%; new cases presented at tumour board 35%; EGFR testing in non-squamous cancer 77%.

audits.intervention: Education and discussion with team members about deviations, with annual audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Histological subtype 100%; tumour board presentation 82%; EGFR testing 100%; staging documented in 100%.

audits.other_findings: Annual audits were run from 2012 to 2015; final-year results given as cycle 2.
audits.citation: Jazieh A, Alkaiyat MO, Ali Y, Hashim MA, Abdelhafiz N, Al Olayan A. Improving adherence to lung cancer guidelines: a quality improvement project that uses chart review, audit and feedback approach. BMJ Open Qual. 2019;8(3):e000436. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2018-000436. PMID: 31523724.

audits.title: Exploring variations in lung cancer care across the UK--the 'story so far' for the National Lung Cancer Audit.
audits.standard: National Lung Cancer Audit process and outcome measures
audits.setting: National Lung Cancer Audit; hospitals in England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Jersey

cycle1.period: Start of the five-year audit period
cycle1.result: Histological confirmation 64%; MDT discussion 78%; anti-cancer treatment 43%; surgical resection 9%; small cell chemotherapy 58%.

audits.intervention: Continuous national audit with feedback over five years.

cycle2.result: Histological confirmation 76%; MDT discussion 94%; anti-cancer treatment 59%; surgical resection 14%; small cell chemotherapy 66%.

audits.other_findings: Audit captures approximately 100% of expected incident cases; national averages hide wide variation between hospitals not explained by casemix.
audits.citation: Beckett P, Woolhouse I, Stanley R, Peake MD. Exploring variations in lung cancer care across the UK--the 'story so far' for the National Lung Cancer Audit. Clin Med (Lond). 2012;12(1):14-18. doi:10.7861/clinmedicine.12-1-14. PMID: 22372213.

audits.title: Nationwide quality improvement in lung cancer care: the role of the Danish Lung Cancer Group and Registry.
audits.standard: National clinical guidelines with process and result indicators
audits.intervention: National guidelines, clinical quality database with quarterly reports and annual formal audit.
audits.other_findings: Improvements in waiting times, cTNM-pTNM accordance and resection rates were also documented; over 40,000 patients registered since 2000.
audits.citation: Jakobsen E, Green A, Oesterlind K, Rasmussen TR, Iachina M, Palshof T. Nationwide quality improvement in lung cancer care: the role of the Danish Lung Cancer Group and Registry. J Thorac Oncol. 2013;8(10):1238-1247. doi:10.1097/jto.0b013e3182a4070f. PMID: 24457234.

audits.title: Changes in the care of non-small-cell lung cancer after audit and feedback: the Florida initiative for quality cancer care.
audits.standard: 16 quality-of-care indicators for non-small-cell lung cancer
audits.setting: 10 oncology practices, Florida Initiative for Quality Cancer Care

cycle1.result: Brain staging for stage III NSCLC 57.8%; chemotherapy flow sheet 89.2%.

audits.intervention: Feedback of 2006 audit results to practices in 2008; practices independently took steps to improve.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in 5 of 16 indicators; brain staging 82.8% (P = .001); chemotherapy flow sheet 97.0%.

audits.citation: Tanvetyanon T, Lee JH, Fulp WJ, Schreiber F, Brown RH, Levine RM, et al.. Changes in the care of non-small-cell lung cancer after audit and feedback: the Florida initiative for quality cancer care. J Oncol Pract. 2014;10(4):e247-54. doi:10.1200/jop.2013.001275. PMID: 24737876.

audits.title: Which patients are assessed by lung cancer nurse specialists? A national lung cancer audit study of over 128,000 patients across england.
audits.standard: NICE recommendation that all lung cancer patients have access to a lung cancer nurse specialist
audits.setting: English National Lung Cancer Audit linked to LCNS workforce census

cycle1.result: LCNS assessment recorded as yes in 62%, no in 6% and missing in 32%.

audits.other_findings: Assessment was lower in older, frailer patients and in high-volume trusts (OR 0.58), and higher where band 8 nurses did most work (OR 2.22).
audits.citation: Khakwani A, Hubbard RB, Beckett P, Borthwick D, Tod A, Leary A, et al.. Which patients are assessed by lung cancer nurse specialists? A national lung cancer audit study of over 128,000 patients across england. Lung Cancer. 2016;96:33-40. doi:10.1016/j.lungcan.2016.03.011. PMID: 27133747.

audits.title: The Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre lung cancer clinical audit: collecting the UK National Lung Cancer Audit data from hospitals in Australia.
audits.standard: UK National Lung Cancer Audit headline indicators (adapted data set)
audits.setting: Six Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre / Western and Central Melbourne Integrated Cancer Service hospitals

cycle1.result: Headline indicators of care were comparable with NLCA data where data completeness was higher; completeness varied significantly between fields.

audits.other_findings: Documented access to specialist lung cancer nurses was lacking.
audits.citation: Mileshkin L, Dunn C, Cross H, Duffy M, Shaw M, Antippa P, et al.. The Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre lung cancer clinical audit: collecting the UK National Lung Cancer Audit data from hospitals in Australia. Intern Med J. 2019;49(8):1001-1006. doi:10.1111/imj.14183. PMID: 30515932.
